A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Residual Connections Harm Generative Representation Learning. All 14 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original MAE representation-learning experiments, diffusion generation results, ablations and supervised feature-rank experiments in Appendix B.2.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and additionally reports ImageNet-1K generation results using SiT-XL/2 and U-ViT-Mid.

M1.justification: Section 5 adds a SiT-XL/2 adaptation with skip connections linking the first half of its layers to the corresponding second half. This is a limited architectural extension; the residual-decay equations, MAE implementation and zero-initialization strategy remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Diffusion evaluation expands from CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100 to full ImageNet-1K class-conditional 256x256 generation with two backbones (v5 Tables 2 and 5). This substantially broadens generation coverage. ImageNet-1K was already used for MAE classification, which remains unchanged.

E2.justification: v5 Table 2 adds comparisons against standard SiT-XL/2 and a SiT-XL/2 control with encoder-decoder skips but no residual decay. The existing MAE comparator set and U-ViT comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The added SiT experiment evaluates 200k and 400k training iterations, reports IS alongside FID, and compares configurations with and without encoder-decoder skips and residual decay. These extend the evaluation protocol; the previously reported MAE and U-ViT settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 Table 2 tests whether SiT gains arise from added skips or residual decay and compares performance at two training budgets. Table 5 extends the decay-factor sweep to ImageNet-1K generation. Existing MAE ablations, reconstruction comparisons and supervised rank analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for these experiments. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Substantial generation results are added. At 400k iterations, v5 Table 2 reports SiT FID values of 17.2 for the baseline, 16.5 with skips alone and 11.8 with decay. Table 5 adds ImageNet-1K U-ViT FIDs of 7.65, 6.23, 5.34 and 4.90 across the decay sweep. These concern added settings; matched earlier numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.3 introduces a deep-linear-encoder assumption, its matrix-product mapping and an argument asserting exponential attenuation of the direct identity contribution. This is a limited theoretical extension without a general proof of the claimed low-rank mechanism. The original method equations and effective-rank definition are unchanged.

C1.justification: v5 removes the dedicated introductory contribution claiming identification of a key low-rank correlation and changes the conclusion to a potential correlation. The abstract still states a correlation, while the main methodological and performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6 softens the attribution of representation improvements to low rank. Appendix B.3 adds an explanation involving weakened identity copying, minimum-norm mappings and denoising-driven covariance concentration. Section 5 also interprets the new SiT controls as attributing most generation gains to residual decay.

D1.justification: v5 adds a code-repository link on page 1 and describes SiT skip wiring and use of its default scheduler and sampler. Appendix A retains the existing MAE hyperparameters, hardware and training-time disclosures.

R1.justification: v5 adds Ma et al.'s SiT paper to support the newly evaluated backbone. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to residual networks, highway networks and low-rank learning remain substantially unchanged; citation renumbering is presentational.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. v5 revises the method introduction and diffusion discussion, updates author affiliations and headings, replaces the generic impact statement with acknowledgments, and adds Appendix B.3. These are localized narrative changes.

P2.justification: The document is globally re-typeset with different headers, typography and display placement. Figures 1 and 2 exchange order, Figure 3 changes from side-by-side grids of 16 examples to enlarged stacked grids of 12, a new SiT table is added, and the diffusion table gains a model column and another dataset row.

improvement.justification: The added ImageNet-1K experiments strengthen evidence that generation benefits extend beyond v4's U-ViT settings, with SiT controls separating residual decay from added skips. The code pointer and qualified correlation claims also help. These are useful incremental gains; Appendix B.3 remains a heuristic mechanism argument, and statistical uncertainty reporting is unchanged.
